In the treatment of oedema the usual oral dose is 5 mg once daily increased according to response to 20 mg once daily; doses of up to 40 mg daily have been re- quired in some patients. Torasemide may also be given intravenously in usual initial doses of 10 to 20 mg daily. Higher doses may sometimes be necessary, espe- cially in oedema of renal origin; the dose should be in- creased stepwise as necessary to a maximum of 200 mg daily, although doses should not exceed 40 mg daily in patients with hepatic cirrhosis. In the treatment of hypertension torasemide is given in initial oral doses of 2.5 to 5 mg daily; US licensed product information allows the dose to be increased to 10 mg daily if required, although UK licensed product information suggests that doses above 5 mg are unlike- ly to produce additional benefit. ◊ Reviews. 1.
